blocks.text: Brutagrafix, also known as Nu-Brutalism, is a modern design aesthetic prominent between the late 2010s and early 2020s that drew inspiration from the 1950s post-war concrete-minimalism architecture that diffuses heavy, raw, architectural motifs with playful, bright, digital graphics. It rejects boring, smooth minimalism to make user interfaces, products and websites look loud, bold and real.
Big Typography: Heavy, large, and raw sans-serif text demands attention.
Hard Shadows: Solid, sharp, offset shadows sit behind shapes instead of blurry, soft gradients.
Bright Colors: Primary colors or high-contrast neon clash against dark or stark white backgrounds.
Thick Outlines: Dark borders or heavy black wrap-around images, buttons, and text boxes.
Nostalgia: Feels a bit like a reminiscence of old-school 1990s internet style mixed with modern polish.
Usability: Unlike messy, older web brutalism, this style keeps clear layouts and normal, user-friendly navigation.
Personality: It stands out in a sea of template-driven, identical websites.
Boxy Layouts: Elements utilize rigid, clear grids and geometric shapes like rectangles and squares.

Anti-design is a graphic design centering around a rebellious visual approach that intentionally rejects traditional rules such as lean grids, symmetry, readability and harmony in favor of colored, chaotic, clashing, and raw unpolished layouts.
Neofolk graphic design blends traditional folk motifs, mystical symbols, and historical aesthetics with modern minimalist or grunge visual systems.
Zinegeist is a visual trend and a graphic design that leans on a DIY scrapbook, raw, and rebellious editorial style. it moves away from clean digital perfection in favor of a tactile, human touch.
Naive design is a visual design trend that utilizes childlike doodles, wobbly lines and intentional imperfection to make digital work feel honest and human.
